examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{残業|ざんぎょう}があります。
{毎日|まいにち}{残業|ざんぎょう}で{疲|つか}れました。
examples.english: I'm tired from overtime every day.

examples.japanese: {残業|ざんぎょう}{代|だい}が{出|で}ますか。
examples.english: Do you get paid for overtime?

examples.japanese: {今月|こんげつ}は{残業|ざんぎょう}が{多|おお}くて{大変|たいへん}です。
examples.english: I have a lot of overtime this month and it's tough.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{残業|ざんぎょう}を{減|へ}らそうとしていますが、{仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わりません。
examples.english: The company is trying to reduce overtime, but the work doesn't get finished.

notes:
{残業|ざんぎょう} means overtime work—working beyond regular hours.

COMPONENTS:
{残|ざん} (remain) + {業|ぎょう} (work) = remaining work

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {残業|ざんぎょう}する: to work overtime
- {残業|ざんぎょう}{代|だい}: overtime pay
- {残業|ざんぎょう}{時間|じかん}: overtime hours
- サービス{残業|ざんぎょう}: unpaid overtime

RELATED TERMS:
- {過労|かろう}: overwork
- {過労死|かろうし}: death from overwork
- {定時|ていじ}: regular hours
- {時間外|じかんがい}{労働|ろうどう}: overtime labor (formal)

WORK REFORM:
{働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく} (work style reform) has been reducing excessive overtime in Japan. Companies now face limits on monthly overtime hours.
